theory.intro: Any angle of the form $180^{\circ}\pm A$ or $360^{\circ}-A$ can be written using its acute **reference angle** $A$. Take the value of the trigonometric ratio at $A$ and attach the sign belonging to its quadrant.
facts: These identities apply for any acute reference angle $A$, with $0^{\circ}<A<90^{\circ}$. For the exact-value tasks here, $A$ is a special angle: $\sin 30^{\circ}=\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\cos 30^{\circ}=\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\tan 30^{\circ}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, $\sin 45^{\circ}=\cos 45^{\circ}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $\tan 45^{\circ}=1$, and the $60^{\circ}$ values swap the $30^{\circ}$ sine and cosine.
A quick sketch of the terminal arm shows the quadrant, so the sign is read straight from ASTC.
steps: Determine the sign from the quadrant

workedExamples.question_text: Write $\cos 230^{\circ}$ as a signed ratio of its acute reference angle. Do not evaluate.
The point $P$ lies on the unit circle at an angle of inclination of $300^{\circ}$. Find its exact coordinates.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Sine is negative in Q3; cosine is positive in Q4.

$\begin{aligned}\sin 240^{\circ}&=-\sin 60^{\circ}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\cos 315^{\circ}&=\cos 45^{\circ}\\&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sin 240^{\circ}+\cos 315^{\circ}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\\&=\frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

foundation.solution_text:
$210^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+30^{\circ}$ lies in the third quadrant, where cosine is negative.
$\cos 210^{\circ}=-\cos 30^{\circ}$
$=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$210^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+30^{\circ}$ lies in the third quadrant, where sine is negative.
$\sin 210^{\circ}=-\sin 30^{\circ}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{2}$

$225^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+45^{\circ}$ lies in the third quadrant, where tangent is positive.
$\tan 225^{\circ}=\tan 45^{\circ}$
$=1$

$300^{\circ}=360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, where sine is negative.
$\sin 300^{\circ}=-\sin 60^{\circ}$
$=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$300^{\circ}=360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, where cosine is positive.
$\cos 300^{\circ}=\cos 60^{\circ}$
$=\dfrac{1}{2}$

$300^{\circ}=360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, where tangent is negative.
$\tan 300^{\circ}=-\tan 60^{\circ}$
$=-\sqrt{3}$

$330^{\circ}=360^{\circ}-30^{\circ}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, where cosine is positive.
$\cos 330^{\circ}=\cos 30^{\circ}$
$=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$240^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+60^{\circ}$ lies in the third quadrant, where sine is negative.
$\sin 240^{\circ}=-\sin 60^{\circ}$
$=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

mastery.question_text:
The point $P$ lies on the unit circle where the radius makes an angle of $315^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis.
Find the exact coordinates of $P$.
mastery.solution_text:
On the unit circle $P=(\cos 315^{\circ},\sin 315^{\circ})$, and $315^{\circ}=360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}$ is in the fourth quadrant.
$\cos 315^{\circ}=\cos 45^{\circ}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\sin 315^{\circ}=-\sin 45^{\circ}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$P=\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
